newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end flat in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end flat in directionless trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat amid virtually no market activity Monday because of the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.
"There were practically no operations today," said an analyst at a large foreign bank. There was no trade in U.S. Treasuries Monday.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at 119.00, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 was steady at 83-1/4.
Traders retained their mainly optimistic views of the market but closer consideration of its failure to rise on Friday when U.S. Treasuries surged led to some disquiet.
Market players said the market fell on profit-taking Friday.

All the same, "the scenario may improve somewhat this week. With a favorable situation in the U.S. Treasury market, Brazil's successful 5-year note and Argentine private pension funds collecting September's contributions, we believe that the market is poised to recover from Friday's levels," said analysts at Banco Republica in an investor note.
Turning to Tuesday, traders said the sale of 250 million pesos in 91-day treasury bill Letes and $500 million in 364-day bills was likely to be the main domestic event of the session.
Analysts and traders estimated a cut-off yield of 7.50 percent for the 91-day peso bills and seven percent for the 364-day dollar bills.
In the money markets, call money rose to 6.55 percent from 6.50 percent Friday.
